full_judgment: The prosecution case was that a holding recorded in Khatian No. 447/10 of Village Jalalabad belonged to the complainant P. W. 1 Aqsad Ali. The rent for the years 1363-66 B. S. of that holding fell in arrear. Certificate Case No. 49119/60-61 was thereupon started and notice thereof was duly served on Aqsad Ali. On 16.6.61 Aqsed Ali remitted the certificate dues amounting to Rs. 18.96 as mentioned in the said notice. This remittance duly reached the office of the Sub-Divisional Manager, who was also the Certificate Officer. lnspite of the receipt of the money, the holding was sold at auction and purchased by the Government. Delivery of possession was taken on behalf of Government by the Tahsildar, that is, the appellant on 17. 11. 62. Thereafter Aqsed Ali submitted a petition on 26. 11. 62 to the Sub-Divisional Manager complaining that inspite of payment of dues, his holding was sold at auction. On that very date (26.11.62) the Nazir of the Sub-Divisional Manager on verification submitted a note to the Sub-Divisional Manager to the effect that the certificate dues were duly received by a money order on 20. 6. 61. The said rote also contained recommendation that the certificate case be shown as satisfied and the certificate costs be realised from the dealing assistant. Aqsed Ali could not, however, know what had happened to his petition addressed to the Sub-Divisional Manager. About one year after, the appellant Tahsildar sent for Aqsed Ali and suggested that he should take fresh settlement of the holding which was auction-purchased in a certificate sale and delivery of possession was taken by Government. He first demanded Rs. 130/- but the amount was settled at Rs. 100/-. Aqsed Ali took time and having borrowed that amount from his relation P. W. 5 Abdur Rahman Gazi met the appellant in the Talisil Office on 4.11. 63. The amount of Rs. 100/- was paid to the appellant who did not grant any receipt to Aqsed Ali on that day. He asked Aqsed Ali to take the receipt 3 or 4 days after. He went to the Tahsil Office as directed. The appellant gave him a dakhila. Aqsed Ali being illiterate showed the dakhila to his neighbour who told him that it was a receipt for Rs. 18.07 only. Thereupon he met the appellant again and asked him as to why receipt was granted for Rs.18.08 and not for Rs. 100/- realised from him. The appellant told him that .06 acre more of his land was made khas by the Government and that he would get settlement of that land as well but the appellant Tahsildar neither gave him the said land nor returned the money. Later Aqsed Ali sent another petition to the Sub-Divisional Manager by registered post on 24. 2.64 informing him of the matter but having received no reply from the office of the Sub-Divisional Manager, he submitted a petition on 7. 4. 65 to the Anti-Corruption Officer at Khulna whereupon an inquiry was held by an Assistant Inspector D. A. B., Sathkhira, who seized the dakhila from Aqsed Ali on 13. 5. 65 and also the records of the certificate case and the other papers from the office of the Sub-Divisional Manager and thereupon a regular case was started at Molaroa Police Station. Having completed the investigation the charge-sheet was submitted upon obtaining sanction from the proper authority.
